title: How Nigerians Abroad Without a BVN Can Invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO
summary: No BVN or Nigerian bank account? Here's how Nigerians in the diaspora can invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO on Bamboo.
body_markdown:
**In short:** If you’re a Nigerian living abroad without a BVN or a Nigerian bank account, you can still invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO on Bamboo through a Nominee Beneficiary account. You’ll need a residential address in Nigeria and a passport, such as your Nigerian passport. Verify your identity, fund your USD wallet through[Misan by Bamboo](https://misan.app.link/NMBL1jwwg6b?%243p=a_custom_1625838821776661357) or a card, and subscribe.


Not having a BVN or a Nigerian bank account used to be a hard stop for Nigerians abroad who wanted in on a Nigerian offer. It no longer is. If you’re Nigerian, living outside the country, and have never gotten around to opening a BVN, Bamboo now lets you invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO through a Nominee Beneficiary account, an alternative route built for exactly this situation.


This guide walks through who this route is for, exactly what you need as a Nigerian in the diaspora, and the steps to apply, based on Bamboo’s official process. It is general information, not investment advice. If you do have a BVN and a Nigerian bank account, the standard route is simpler, and our guide on[how to invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO on Bamboo](https://learn.investbamboo.com/how-to-invest-in-the-dangote-refinery-ipo-on-bamboo-a-step-by-step-guide/) covers that path. If you are a non-Nigerian African looking to invest, a separate guide covers that route.


## What is a Nominee Beneficiary account?


A Nominee Beneficiary account, also known as Bamboo’s NGX Nominee Account, is an alternative way for Nigerians without a BVN or a Nigerian bank account to invest in NGX IPOs on Bamboo. Under this structure, Bamboo holds the investment through its own nominee account on the NGX and registers you as the beneficiary, in line with the account’s terms and conditions. You still own the economic benefit of the shares; Bamboo simply holds them on your behalf as the nominee.


This is what makes it possible to skip the two things that normally gate Nigerian investing: a BVN and a Nigerian bank account.


## What you need


- **Your Nigerian international passport** (or another supported passport, if applicable to you).
- **Your Nigerian address** .
- **A phone number** you can receive a verification code on.
- **A way to fund a USD wallet** , such as a Misan virtual account, or a USD debit or credit card.
- **At least $100** , the minimum deposit to fund your USD wallet.


## Step by step: how to apply


1. **[Download the Bamboo app](https://investbamboo.app.link/dangote-ipo-articles?%243p=a_custom_1626873672854248151)** from the App Store or Google Play.
2. **Tap “Invest in Dangote IPO”** on the app’s landing screen, or start creating your account and look for the same option.
3. **Select your citizenship.** As a Nigerian, this will typically be Nigeria, using your Nigerian passport to verify your identity.
4. **Provide your address.** Enter your country, state, and full Nigerian address.
5. **Verify your identity.** Scan your passport, then take a clear selfie photo when prompted. Good lighting and no blur make this faster.
6. **Set a 4-digit PIN** to secure your account.
7. **Provide next-of-kin details** , including their name, relationship to you, and phone number.
8. **Complete your investment profile.** Answer a short set of questions covering your employment, marital status, investment goal, timeline, experience, and risk tolerance. This personalises your account and is a standard part of onboarding.
9. **Wait for verification.** Your account may show as under review while Bamboo checks your details. This does not usually take long, but it is a real step, not a formality, so give it a moment before assuming something has gone wrong.
10. **Fund your USD wallet.** Once verified, add at least $100 to your USD wallet using Misan or a USD debit or credit card.
11. **Subscribe to the Dangote Refinery IPO.** From your home screen or the Assets tab, tap the “Dangote IPO now live” banner, choose how many shares you want (minimum 10 at ₦525 each), select your payment method, and confirm.


## Funding your USD wallet


You have two main ways to fund your wallet.


**[Misan](https://misan.app.link/NMBL1jwwg6b?%243p=a_custom_1625838821776661357)** , Bamboo’s own remittance app, lets you fund via bank transfer using a personal virtual account, in USD, GBP, EUR, or CAD. It carries small deposit fees depending on currency, for example around 0.1% on GBP and EUR transfers and 0.5% on USD transfers, each with a modest minimum and maximum. Your virtual account is usually ready within about an hour, sometimes longer depending on verification checks. For a Nigerian abroad who already earns in one of these currencies, this is often the simplest way to get money into your Bamboo wallet without an unnecessary conversion.


**A USD debit or credit card** through Paystack or Flutterwave is the faster option if you already have one, though card funding carries a processing fee from the payment provider, typically around 2.9%.


Either way, funding your wallet is a separate step from investing. Subscribing to the Dangote Refinery IPO itself carries zero commission on Bamboo; the fees above belong to the funding method you choose to get money into your wallet, not to the investment.


## What happens after you apply


Once you’ve subscribed, there’s nothing further to do until allotment. Our guide on[what happens after you apply for the Dangote Refinery IPO](https://learn.investbamboo.com/dangote-refinery-ipo-everything-you-need-to-know/) covers the full timetable, but in brief: after the offer closes, the SEC clears the Basis of Allotment, your shares are credited, and if you were allotted fewer shares than you applied for, or none, the difference is returned to your Bamboo wallet automatically.


If you ever want to move money from your USD wallet back to your bank account, be aware that withdrawals carry a $45 fee and typically take five to seven business days to arrive, so plan around that rather than treating your wallet as instantly accessible.


## A word on getting this right


Only invest money you can afford to have tied up and, ultimately, to lose. Never borrow to fund an application, and always apply through the official Bamboo app rather than any third party claiming to help you “get in” from abroad. Our[Don’ts of Investing](https://learn.investbamboo.com/the-donts-of-investing-10-things-nigerian-investors-should-never-do/) series covers these principles in more depth.


## Frequently asked questions


**Can a Nigerian abroad invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO without a BVN?** Yes, through a Nominee Beneficiary account on Bamboo. You’ll need a residential address in a Nigeria and a passport, such as your Nigerian passport, instead of a BVN and a Nigerian bank account.


**What is a Nominee Beneficiary account?** An arrangement where Bamboo holds your investment through its nominee account on the NGX and registers you as the beneficiary, so you don’t need a BVN or Nigerian bank account to invest.


**I live outside Nigeria and don’t have a Nigerian address. Can I still use this?** Not yet. You can sign up and browse the app from many countries outside Africa, but completing identity verification for this route currently requires a residential address in a supported African country. If you have a BVN and a Nigerian bank account, use the standard route instead.


**How much does it cost to invest this way?** Subscribing to the Dangote Refinery IPO carries zero commission. Funding your USD wallet may carry a small fee depending on the method: Misan charges a small percentage with a minimum and maximum depending on currency, and card funding through Paystack or Flutterwave carries a processing fee of around 2.9%.


**What is the minimum I need to invest?** The IPO minimum is 10 shares at ₦525 each. Separately, your USD wallet needs at least $100 to be funded before you can subscribe.


**How do I fund my wallet with foreign currency?** Use Misan, Bamboo’s remittance app, which supports USD, GBP, EUR, and CAD, or fund with a USD card through Paystack or Flutterwave.

## Ready to get started?


No BVN, no problem.[Download the Bamboo app](https://investbamboo.app.link/dangote-ipo-articles?%243p=a_custom_1626873672854248151) and start your Nominee Beneficiary application today. The Dangote Refinery IPO window closes on 13 October 2026.


### Quick Summary


This guide explains how Nigerians in the diaspora who do not have a BVN or a Nigerian bank account can invest in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals IPO, using Bamboo's Nominee Beneficiary account, also known as the NGX Nominee Account. Under this structure, Bamboo holds the investment through its nominee account and registers the investor as the beneficiary. To use it, a Nigerian abroad needs a residential address in Nigeria and their Nigerian international passport. The process involves selecting citizenship, providing an African address, verifying identity with a passport and photo, setting a PIN, providing next-of-kin details, and completing a short investment profile. Once verified, investors fund a USD wallet, minimum $100, using Misan (Bamboo's remittance app, supporting USD, GBP, EUR, and CAD with small deposit fees) or a USD debit or credit card, and then subscribe to the Dangote Refinery IPO at ₦525 per share with a minimum of 10 shares, with zero commission on the investment itself.
